story_title: A Day at the Amusement Park
paragraphs: Our class visits an amusement park for a science-themed school trip. The first ride {{mask_1}} we try travels slowly through a model solar system. The guide points out a planet {{mask_2}} has rings made of ice and rock. The main entrance, {{mask_3}} was rebuilt last year, has a wide glass roof. We read a sign {{mask_4}} explains how the ride uses magnets.

After the ride, we explore an interactive science pavilion. A machine {{mask_5}} measures the force of a visitor's push displays the result on a screen. The pavilion, {{mask_6}} stands beside the lake, also has a small planetarium. Inside, we watch a film {{mask_7}} follows a spacecraft on its journey. The seats, {{mask_8}} can lean back, make it easy to look up at the ceiling.

At lunchtime, our teacher leads us to a picnic area. We choose a table {{mask_9}} is near a fountain. The fountain, {{mask_10}} was designed by a local artist, changes color in the afternoon. A food stall {{mask_11}} sells vegetable wraps has a short line. The menu, {{mask_12}} lists ingredients for each dish, helps students with food allergies.

In the afternoon, we visit the park's engineering workshop. The model bridge {{mask_13}} the students build must hold a small toy train. A technician, {{mask_14}} works at the park, shows us how to test the supports. We use a tool {{mask_15}} measures the bridge's strength. The workshop, {{mask_16}} opened earlier this spring, is popular with school groups.

Before we leave, we watch a parade near the central plaza. The floats {{mask_17}} move along the main path carry bright decorations. A dragon float, {{mask_18}} has lights inside its wings, is the children's favorite. Our teacher takes a photo, {{mask_19}} includes the whole class. The park, {{mask_20}} welcomes thousands of visitors each year, has given us plenty to discuss on the bus ride home.
